title: The role of RNA m6A modification in the regulation of HIV latency and reactivation
text:
Our understanding of HIV latency and persistence has been complicated by the small numbers
of latently infected cells in vivo. This project develops highly sensitive assays to measure m6A
RNA modifications in HIV RNA in patient samples and informative primary cell models for HIV
latency to study the epitranscriptomic regulation of HIV transcription.

title: Unraveling Counter-Regulatory Transcriptional Control by the ZBED Family in Beta Cell Stress and Immune Tolerance
text:
By integrating in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening, transcriptomic profiling, and functional analyses,
we identified the ZBED transcription factor family as regulators of beta cell genes involved in interferon signaling,
stress adaptation, and functional identity. This proposal investigates the reciprocal roles of ZBED2 and ZBED3
in shaping beta cell stress responses and immune tolerance in the context of type 1 diabetes. The findings will
establish a transcriptional framework for beta cell resilience and guide the development of next-generation cell
replacement strategies that complement existing immune-based therapies.

title: Tumor Biology
text: Program Summary/Abstract The overall goal of the Dan L Duncan Comprehensive Cancer Center's (DLDCCC) Tumor Biology (TB) Program is to uncover new cancer cell-intrinsic and extrinsic factors that drive tumor development, progression metastasis and therapeutic resistance. The TB Program has 50 research and 10 clinical members with over $26 million in total direct funding and more than $6 million from the NCI. During the funding period, Program members published 683 papers, 11% in journals with impact factors >20, demonstrating robust intra-programmatic (24%), inter-programmatic (36%), and inter-institutional (64%) collaborations. The Program is focused on two overarching scientific themes - Cancer Progression and the Microenvironment - that support a systems biology approach to understand tumor biology as a whole and translate discoveries to therapeutic approaches. Several teams of investigators approach these themes using genomics, proteomics and mathematical modeling approaches, as well as drug discovery and understanding signal transduction networks. Extrinsic tumor microenvironment studies focus on immunology, reactive stroma, metabolism, and the microbiome. Our basic research has led to the identification of cross-cutting biological mechanisms in several cancer types, modeling that predicts driver genes, and drug discovery to target progression. Microenvironment studies have led to new vaccine and immunotherapy approaches, paradigm-changing real-time mass spectrometry MasSpec Pen technology to evaluate tumor margins, and identification of new metabolic markers that help identify the biological basis of differences in health care outcomes. Together, these studies have identified several actionable targets, leading to the initiation of clinical trials focused on pancreatic cancer, head and neck cancer, and mesothelioma, in line with the strategic goals of the DLDCCC. In addition, studies have led to translation of multi-omics through generation of comprehensive proteogenomic databases. These contributions have substantially advanced our understanding of cancer, improved data analysis methodologies, and broadened data accessibility for the scientific community. The TB Program has successfully conducted and translated basic research to the bedside and will continue to promote these efforts by working closely with the Translational Working Groups to efficiently bring basic discoveries forward to clinical trials. Promoting communication and interactions is another strength of the TB Program, and we will continue to leverage DLDCCC Shared Resources to support members in achieving program goals.

title: CSHL 2026 Conference on Cell and Membrane Fusion
text:
This conference brings together scientists studying how cells and their membranes fuse together, a fundamental
process required for muscle formation and repair, bone health, fertility, and fighting viral infections.
Understanding these fusion mechanisms is essential for developing treatments for muscular dystrophy,
osteoporosis, and infertility. By fostering collaboration between many different researchers, this meeting will
accelerate discoveries that lead to new knowledge in muscle and bone biology.

title: Hyper-surveillance and suicides among Black youth in the U.S.
text: The proposed work examines the association between patterns of police stop activity and suicide-related outcomes among Black youth using a longitudinal, ecological approach. This project may help clarify the association between intensive law enforcement practices and adverse mental health outcomes.

title: Genetic modifiers of congenital heart disease in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
text:
This project will take human and animal model genetic approaches to understand the basis of phenotypic
variability of congenital heart disease among 22q11.2 deletion syndrome patients. We will analyze whole
genome sequence from subjects with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome with/out congenital heart defects and
validate discoveries in mouse and zebrafish models. Some of the genes studied may also be risk factors for
sporadic congenital heart disease in the general population.

title: Deciphering Cytokine Regulation of Lymphocyte Trafficking
text:
The mammalian body is monitored by migratory lymphocytes that travel via the blood to lymph nodes and
Peyer's patches to find antigens, relying on high endothelial venules (HEV) for this process. HEV can also
arise in chronic inflammation and tumors where they facilitate lymphocyte accumulation in tertiary lymphoid
structures that can worsen inflammation or improve tumor response to immunotherapy. This project aims to
explore how endothelial cell signaling through CD130, its ligands and co-receptors, LIFR and OSMR, impacts
HEV formation and maintenance, potentially revealing new targets for treating cancer and inflammatory
diseases.

title: Preclinical Molecular Imaging (PMI)
text: The Preclinical Molecular Imaging Shared Resource (PMI-SR), previously called Preclinical Imaging and Computational Analysis, was established in 1986 and has been continuously funded by the Cancer Center Support Grant (CCSG) since 1988. To optimize growth and development, PMI-SR provides Rogel members access to state-of-the-art imaging instrumentation including positron emission tomography (PET), 3T and 7T magnetic resonance scanners, 3D and 4D computed tomography (CT) scanners, and bioluminescence/ fluorescence IVIS systems. Moreover, PMI-SR provides the indispensable scientific expertise to assist investigators with study design and interpretation of results. PMI-SR supports basic science studies along with proof of principle studies for eventual integration of imaging into clinical translational studies for further validation and to serve as companion diagnostics and predictive markers.

title: Lateral Hypothalamic circuit dysfunction underlying the development of diet-induced obesity
text:
Changes in brain function are thought to underlie the development of obesity and type 2 diabetes. Neurons
located in the lateral hypothalamic area control feeding behavior, energy homeostasis, and body weight, but their
role in the development of obesity is unclear. Addressing lateral hypothalamic involvement in overeating will help
us understand the neurocircuit mechanisms that control diet-induced obesity and will inform future therapeutic
interventions.

title: Auditory cortical processing of self-generated sounds
text:
During sound-guided behaviors like speech and musicianship, we listen to the sounds that our actions produce,
we compare what we heard with what we expected to hear, and we detect mismatches between expectation and
experience. Although errors are instrumental for behaviors like speech and music, the neural circuits that
integrate motor, acoustic, and goal-related signals to detect errors and guide learning in mammals are unknown.
Here, we will test the hypothesis that the mouse auditory cortex integrates sound and behavior-related signals
during skilled acoustic behaviors, detects errors, and routes error-related signals to motor regions of the brain to
adapt subsequent acoustic behaviors.

title: Epigenetic Biomarkers in Glioblastoma
text:
GBM is currently incurable although there is promise of using CAR-T cell therapy if we understand the molecular
underpinnings of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment. We have discovered a novel pathway that controls
the levels of antigens on tumor cells to allow them to be recognized by CAR-T cells. Our proposed studies will
define a novel biomarker for GBM therapy in immunotherapy clinical trials.

title: Visual Science Training Program
text:
The overall goal of the Visual Science Training Program (VSTP) is to recruit talented young
researchers both pre- and postdoctoral fellows and provide them a broad research training with
an overall emphasis on vision loss in the context of human disease, which will enable them to
discover new horizons and contribute to our understanding of the biology of the visual cascade
and the underlying pathologies resulting in loss of vision.

title: Ultra-high precision image-guided incisionless transcranial ultrasound surgery
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Building on our work developing volumetric super‐resolution ultrasound imaging and dual‐frequency therapeutic
arrays for glioblastoma, this supplement will overcome local compute bottlenecks by deploying scalable cloud
and hybrid resources to accelerate full‐wave acoustic simulations, 3D beamforming, and high‐rate super‐
resolution reconstruction across terabyte‐scale datasets. By porting our simulation and image‐processing
pipelines into GPU‐enabled cloud clusters with automated benchmarking, we will systematically optimize array
designs, skull aberration correction strategies, and nonlinear filtering methods, enabling efficient exploration of
imaging and therapy parameters across diverse anatomical models. These high‐throughput, reproducible
workflows will facilitate real‐time microvascular mapping and functional imaging, refine vascular biomarker
identification and personalized treatment planning, and establish a robust blueprint for scalable cloud‐enabled
ultrasound research.

title: Defining mechanisms of disease and repair in a viral model of multiple sclerosis
text:
An important unmet clinical need for MS patients is an effective method for promoting
remyelination that can ameliorate clinical symptoms associated with demyelination and restore motor
function while limiting immune cell infiltration into the CNS. Using a well-accepted preclinical animal
model for MS, key areas of research include identifying signaling pathways governing neuroinflammation,
characterizing signaling pathways controlling oligodendroglia maturation and remyelination, and
refinement of strategies to improve neural progenitor cell (NPC)-mediated remyelination following surgical
engraftment into the CNS and how non-coding RNAs influence disease. In addition, we will employ state-
of-the-art single cell and nuclear RNA sequencing to better understand how immune cells interact with
resident cells of the CNS during demyelination and remyelination.

title: Novel CAR T cell engineering strategies for effective eradication of solid and liquid tumors
text:
Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells are a cancer therapy that reprograms patient immune cells to
kill cancer cells. They have cured many blood cancer patients but require optimization to effectively
treat patients who are initially resistant to this therapy or have other tumor types. We will use novel
engineering strategies to improve CAR T cell function and make them effective for these patients.

title: Exosome Mediated Effects on Cardiac Injury during Cardiopulmonary Bypass
text:
There is a 20% chance of a decrease in left ventricular function after surgical correction of primary mitral
regurgitation (PMR). This grant will utilize cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and acute cardiac and kidney
injury during cardiopulmonary bypass to predict a fall in left ventricular function after surgery to correct PMR.

title: Distinct Ion Channel Pools and Intercalated Disk Nanoscale Structure Regulate Cardiac Conduction
text:
Several electrogenic proteins critical for electrical excitation in cardiac tissue (including voltage-gated
sodium channels, inward-rectifying potassium channels, L-type calcium channels, the sodium-
potassium ATPase, and the sodium-calcium exchanger) reside in distinct ion channel “pools” within
cells, with a subset of these channels critical for conduction preferentially localized at the site of cell-
cell junctions, the intercalated disk. While recent evidence suggests that cardiac conduction is sensitive
to perturbations at the intercalated disk, the contributions of these distinct ion channel pools and the
intercalated disk nanoscale structure in regulating conduction under both normal and pathological
conditions are not fully understood. We hypothesize that distinct ion channel pools on the lateral
membrane and both at and within the intercalated disk, and intercalated disk structure constitute the
key components of a “global/local control” system that regulate robust cardiac conduction, mitigating
sensitivity to changes in ion channel and gap junction expression, and that this system of regulation is
disrupted during pathological settings, including non-ischemic heart failure.

title: Investigating Autism-Related Gut Dysfunction with Human Enteric Neurons and Intestinal Organoids
text:
This project is highly relevant to public health, given the high prevalence of gastrointestinal disorders in
individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the current gap in knowledge regarding the contribution of
specific cell types in ASD-associated GI dysfunction. By utilizing a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-
derived Enteric Neurons (ENs) and intestinal organoids, this project dissects the contribution of ENs from those
of other intestinal cells to the overall disease phenotype across multiple ASD-associated genes. This research
offers a unique approach to dissecting insights into the complex relationship between human ENs and autism-
related gut dysfunction, presenting potential avenues for refining healthcare strategies.

title: Facilitating the Advancement of Research and Education for Undergraduate Students by Incorporating Laser Scanning Confocal Microscopy (FAREUS-LSCM)
text:
The acquisition of a laser-scanning confocal microscope will significantly enhance UPR-
Aguadilla’s research capacity in public health-relevant fields, including host-parasite interactions,
immune responses, agricultural pathogens, environmental pollutants, and neurological disorders
linked to diabetes. This advanced imaging technology will provide biology students-many of whom
pursue careers in biomedical fields-with hands-on training using tools commonly found in
research hospitals and biotech industries. By integrating cutting-edge microscopy into
undergraduate education, the institution will better prepare students for competitive graduate
programs and careers in medicine, biomedical research, and public health.

title: Zebrafish Development and Genetics
text:
Over the past 25 years, the zebrafish has become one of the most prominent model systems in which to study
the genetic, molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying embryonic development, regeneration, and
disease. This proposal requests support for an intensive two-week laboratory and lecture course held at the
Marine Biological Laboratory (MBL) for advanced graduate students, postdoctoral fellows and independent
investigators that focuses on the development and genetics of zebrafish, with special emphasis on early
embryogenesis, models of birth defects, and regeneration. In its 24th year, the MBL Zebrafish course is the
only course of its kind worldwide, and it consistently receives rave reviews from participants, many of whom
consider their experience in the course as instrumental in starting their own zebrafish research program.
